subject: Biology
source: IISER IAT 2026, final answer key (English), iiseradmission.in
_transcription: Biology = pages p02-p17 (p01 is the cover/note page). Printed numbers 1-15, one question per page from p02 to p06 and p08 to p17; p07 has no question number: it is the continuation of Q5 (its option (c) and (d) graphs). Numbers checked unbroken 1..15 against the 'N. Question N' headings. Q2's match table is printed as a picture and typed as a pipe table. Q11's four lac operon schematics are rows of labelled boxes and are typed (box labels left to right), not cropped. Q13's options are printed as pictures of sequences; the sequences are typed exactly and the pictures are also given as option figures. Stem figures: Q3 (p04 graphs), Q8 (p10 gene diagram), Q14 (p16 pedigree). Picture options: Q5 (p06 a-b, p07 c-d), Q13 (p15).

rows.text:
Which of the following processes result in development of a proton gradient across the thylakoid membrane during photosynthesis?

i. Release of protons into the lumen of the thylakoid by plastoquinone
ii. Consumption of protons in the stroma during the reduction of NADP\(^+\)
iii. Release of protons into the lumen of the thylakoid by ATP synthase
iv. Release of protons into the lumen of the thylakoid by water splitting reaction

Which one of the following choices matches the organs in column I with their vascular system arrangement described in column II?

| | Column I | | Column II |
|---|---|---|---|
| P. | Dicot root | i. | Radial, open, diarch to tetrarch |
| Q. | Dicot stem | ii. | Ring, conjoint, open |
| R. | Monocot root | iii. | Radial, closed, polyarch |
| S. | Monocot stem | iv. | Scattered, conjoint, closed |

The graphs below depict the number of individuals of two organisms, named P and Q, when grown independently, and together. Based on these growth patterns, which one of the following statements is correct?
options: Q is a predator of P
P is a parasite of Q
Q is a commensal of P

figure.note: Three graphs, each with y-axis 'Number of individuals' and x-axis 'Time'. 'Growth of P': solid curve rising from the origin and levelling off to a plateau. 'Growth of Q': dashed curve rising from the origin and levelling off to a plateau. 'Growth of P and Q together': dashed curve labelled Q rising steadily to a plateau; thick solid curve labelled P rising faster at first to a peak (where it meets the Q curve) and then falling to zero.

rows.text: The pBR322 cloning vector has genes coding for tetracycline and ampicillin resistance. A foreign DNA to be cloned is inserted into the tetracycline resistance gene and the recombinant plasmid is then transformed into E. coli cells. Which one of the following choices is the most likely outcome of this cloning reaction?
options: The cells with the recombinant plasmid can grow in the presence of ampicillin but not tetracycline
The cells with the recombinant plasmid can grow in the presence of both ampicillin and tetracycline
The cells with the non-recombinant plasmid can grow in the presence of ampicillin but not tetracycline
The cells with the non-recombinant plasmid can grow in the presence of tetracycline but not ampicillin

rows.text: Which one of the following correctly describes the mode of action of Follicle Stimulating Hormone (FSH) and estrogen?
options: FSH interacts with membrane-bound receptor and generates cyclic AMP, while estrogen interacts with intracellular receptor and regulates gene expression
FSH interacts with intracellular receptor and generates cyclic AMP, while estrogen interacts with membrane-bound receptor and regulates cellular metabolism
Both FSH and estrogen regulate gene expression via intracellular receptors
Both FSH and estrogen regulate cellular metabolism via membrane-bound receptors

rows.text: Which one of the following correctly describes the sequence of events leading to muscle contraction following acetylcholine release at the neuromuscular junction?
options: Increase of \(\mathrm{Ca^{++}}\) in sarcoplasm, unmasking of active sites for myosin, 'Z' lines pulled inwards
Increase of \(\mathrm{Ca^{++}}\) in sarcoplasm, masking of active sites for myosin, 'Z' lines pulled inwards
Increase of \(\mathrm{Ca^{++}}\) in sarcoplasm, unmasking of active sites for myosin, 'Z' lines pulled outwards
Decrease of \(\mathrm{Ca^{++}}\) in sarcoplasm, masking of active sites for myosin, 'Z' lines pulled inwards

rows.text: In which one of the following cases, will an anti-Rh antibody treatment prevent erythroblastosis foetalis?
options: Anti-Rh antibody to the Rh-negative mother after delivery of the first Rh-positive child
Anti-Rh antibody to the Rh-positive mother after delivery of the first Rh-negative child
Anti-Rh antibody to the Rh-negative mother after delivery of the first Rh-negative child
Anti-Rh antibody to the Rh-positive mother after delivery of the first Rh-positive child

The following pedigree diagram shows the inheritance of a rare genetic disorder in a family (filled shapes depict affected individuals). Which one of the following is the most likely pattern of inheritance of the disorder?

figure.note: Four-generation pedigree (squares male, circles female, filled = affected). Generation I: unaffected female x affected male. Their six children, left to right: affected female (married to an unaffected male), unaffected male, affected female (married to an unaffected male), unaffected male, unaffected male (married to an unaffected female), affected female. Children of the first affected daughter: affected male (married to an unaffected female), unaffected male, unaffected female, affected female. Children of the second affected daughter: unaffected female, unaffected male, affected female, affected male (married to an unaffected female). Children of the married unaffected son: unaffected female, unaffected male, unaffected male, unaffected female. Generation IV, children of the first affected grandson: affected female, unaffected male, affected female, affected female, unaffected male. Children of the second affected grandson: affected female, affected female, unaffected male, affected female, unaffected male.
